entities.evidence: In הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, “the mountains of Ararat,” Ararat names the region where the ark came to rest. The source tag identifies the same place.

review.translation: [And|0] [in|2] [the seventh|3] [month|2], [on|4] [the seventeenth|4,5] [day|6] [of the month|7], [the ark|1] [came to rest|0] [on|8] [the mountains of|9] [Ararat|10].

analysis.evidence: וַתָּנַח agrees with its feminine singular subject הַתֵּבָה, “the ark.” The phrase עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, “on the mountains of Ararat,” identifies where the ark came to rest.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

draft.change: Add תֵּבָה under its own consonants תבה, with evidence for Noah’s ark and the smaller container used for Moses.
draft.definition: A waterproofed container that holds people or animals on water. Here it is Noah’s ark.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:14 describes the ark’s construction and sealing with pitch. Genesis 7:18 describes it floating, and Genesis 8:4 records where it came to rest.

analysis.evidence: הַתֵּבָה is the subject of וַתָּנַח, “came to rest,” which agrees with it in the feminine singular. עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט gives the place where the ark came to rest after floating on the waters in Genesis 7:18.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ with doubling of the initial ת, followed by a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carried Noah, his household, and the animals on the floodwaters.

analysis.evidence: הַשְּׁבִיעִי modifies חֹדֶשׁ to give “in the seventh month,” and בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ specifies the seventeenth day of that month.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי, “in the seventh month,” the ordinal agrees with חֹדֶשׁ in gender, number, and definiteness. The following phrase gives the day of that month.
analysis.morphology: Ordinal adjective, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעָה supplies the seven in שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר, “seventeen,” which counts the masculine noun יוֹם. The prefixed בְּ marks the date on which the ark rested, the seventeenth day of the month.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ prefixed to שִׁבְעָה, a masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral.

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, עָשָׂר supplies the ten and שִׁבְעָה supplies the seven. Together they date the ark’s resting to the seventeenth day of the month.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, יוֹם is the unit counted by שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר ‘seventeen’. The phrase dates the ark’s resting to the seventeenth day of the seventh month.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ means “on the seventeenth day of the month.” The article refers back to the seventh month named earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ with the definite article הַ, prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, עַל identifies where the ark came to rest: on the mountains of Ararat.
In עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, “on the mountains of Ararat,” הָרֵי is bound to the place name אֲרָרָט. The phrase locates the ark’s resting place.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural construct, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a geographical name article keyed by the name’s own consonants, אררט.
draft.definition: Ararat is the region whose mountains are named as the ark’s resting place.
draft.evidence: Gen.8.4 locates the ark עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, “on the mountains of Ararat.”

analysis.evidence: In עַל הָרֵי אֲרָרָט, “on the mountains of Ararat,” הָרֵי is the plural construct of הַר, “mountain.” אֲרָרָט names the region to which those mountains belong. The verse gives no basis for deriving the name from ארר or glossing it as “wrath.”
analysis.morphology: Geographical proper noun, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase הָרֵי אֲרָרָט.
analysis.sense: Ararat, the region whose mountains are named as the ark’s resting place.
